message.content:
The number of distinct positions that can arise in a standard game of chess (starting from the initial arrangement) is astronomically large.  In fact, the best estimates put it at roughly

\[
10^{46}\text{ – }10^{47}
\]

legal positions.

This figure is often referred to as the **Shannon number** (≈ 10^43), which is a lower bound on the number of possible positions.  More recent analyses and computational studies suggest that the true count is closer to 10^46, though an exact value has not yet been proven.  Thus, while the exact number remains unknown, we know that there are on the order of tens of quadrillion quadrillion legal positions in chess.
